idiom_name: EF Core navigation property plus foreign key property (HasForeignKey)
implementation_notes: EF Core models the association as a navigation property (Post.Blog) plus a foreign key property (Post.BlogId) that the context keeps in sync; HasOne/WithMany/HasForeignKey configures the relationship explicitly when convention is not enough, and the key property does not have to be a visible CLR member - it still exists in the EF model and drives SQL generation. The framework replaces the classic mapper: SaveChanges writes the referenced entity's key into the column, and query fix-up wires the object references back through the change tracker. Hand-written ADO.NET/Dapper mapping of a BlogId column remains justified when the model must stay free of EF and mapping metadata, or for one hot query that should not go through the tracker.
pitfalls: An FK property hidden from the CLR type (an EF shadow property) makes seeding and detached-graph updates guesswork: a detached Post with a wrong BlogId attaches to the wrong parent without any error.

Lazy loading needs virtual navigations and the proxy package; without them an unfixed-up reference is simply null, so code that assumed lazy resolution throws NullReferenceException at the worst moment.
EF trusts client-set FK values, so a request-supplied BlogId must be authorised against the parent, not just checked for existence.
